claim: A 1-min spike (volume >= 8x, move >= 5 sigma) in top-dollar-volume names keeps running for the next hour in the afternoon.
evidence: SIP 2022-26 top 25: +15.8 bps, t 2.7. IEX detection keeps about half (+7..10 gross). All years +7.1 net, t 3.08, n=1485. Live pod since 2026-10-30, too few trades to judge.
reopen_if: Live plus shadow evidence averages under the pause rule after 30+ trades.

claim: Spike P&L comes from a small share of trades; the median trade loses a little.
evidence: Median -0.8 bps, win rate 48%, top 1% of trades = 45-63% of P&L. Never split by event days.

claim: Adding names beyond the top 25 by dollar volume improves the spike pod.
evidence: Rank 26-100 held out +3.3 bps net, t 1.28, 2 of 5 years. With the 4-position cap, weak names crowd out better ones.
reopen_if: A filter separates the good signals among those names.

claim: Bigger spikes (sigma or volume) run further.
evidence: Design big-small +17.3 bps (t 3.29), held out -1.2. The biggest-volume third is the worst held out.
reopen_if: News or event conditioning changes what size means.

claim: A learned exit beats the fixed 60-minute hold.
evidence: Top 25: +1.9 bps held out, t 1.35. Wider names: -1.2 held out, -0.9 fresh. In-sample fitting.
reopen_if: New inputs (news, regime) exist that the first tests lacked.

claim: Kronos-small adds tradable information, alone or as a filter.
evidence: Standalone best +3.1 bps gross. As a spike filter, disagreeing beat agreeing by about 11 bps in both windows, t < 2.
reopen_if: The disagreement effect is tested and pre-registered as its own idea.

claim: Opening-range breakouts have an edge at real costs, fixed list or stocks in play.
evidence: A few bps gross. Live since 9/14, paused 11/02.
reopen_if: A regime or news filter passes on it as a pre-registered test.

claim: Gap continuation, including SSR-filtered short gaps, pays at real costs.
evidence: Best +0.13R at 5 bps, 3 of 5 windows. Rerun at lower costs doesn't flip it.
reopen_if: Gap cause (news type) can be separated.

claim: The first half hour predicts the index's last half hour after costs.
evidence: No edge at real costs, including 0.5 bps.
reopen_if: Only with a new conditioning variable.

claim: Fading short-term moves pays: spike_fade, vwap_fade, RSI2, weekly reversal.
evidence: Fades negative. RSI2 +6 bps excess is under 10 bps cost. Weekly reversal -4.9 excess, t -1.0; held out +4.0, t 0.9.
reopen_if: Split by news vs no news, which theory says matters (ideas.md 11 is a related volatility split).

claim: Earnings dates give a daily-bar edge: post-earnings drift or pre-earnings run-up.
evidence: PEAD on real 8-K dates: excess -29..+13 bps, no t > 2.5. Run-up -14 bps, t -4.7, held out the same.
reopen_if: Earnings surprise size or text is available, since dates alone carried nothing.

claim: Any big move on heavy volume drifts afterwards.
evidence: No excess vs the pool. Event drifts in liquid names price in within a session.

claim: Holding liquid names close-to-open only earns enough to trade.
evidence: About +2 bps gross a night vs 4 bps round trip, faded since 2021, negative every year hedged against SPY.
reopen_if: A cross-sectional signal earns well over 4 bps (ideas.md 10).

claim: Stocks earn outsized returns around the month turn, tradably.
evidence: The 62 excess -7.2 bps, t -1.04. Timing +8.3, t 0.46, driven by 2020.

claim: The near-misses only fail because of costs.
evidence: Rerun with limit-order costs: nothing flips. The signals themselves are weak.

claim: Inverse-volatility weighting beats equal weight across pods.
evidence: Spike vs sleeve 2018-26: Sharpe 1.01, max drawdown -6.9% vs 0.94, -16.9%. Only two streams.
reopen_if: Retest when three pods are live.

claim: New edge in these liquid names is more likely from new data (news, filings, flows, options) than from more price rules.
evidence: 11 straight FAILs, nearly all price patterns on the same data. A pattern, not a test; the news and filing tests will challenge it.
reopen_if: New-data tests fail as often as price tests have: rethink the universe and horizon instead.

claim: The 1-min cache is unadjusted, so tests held across an overnight must filter splits.
evidence: GE's 1:8 reverse split scored +682% in the first turn-of-month run. Overnight-drift wasn't filtered; about -1.4 bps a name-night, verdict unchanged.
